'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Battle of Kharkiv (2022)|Battle of Kharkiv]]
****The [[Albania]]n [[consulate]] in [[Kharkiv]] is destroyed during Russian shelling. No casualties are reported. [https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/short_news/russian-strike-in-ukraine-destroys-albanian-consulate/ (Euractiv)]
***[[White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] reaffirms that the [[United States|U.S.]] will not impose a [[no-fly zone]] over [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/russia-ukraine-latest-news-2022-03-08/card/white-house-downplays-chances-of-limited-no-fly-zone-in-ukraine-9Wn0MC7iDffSinjV5oQw (''Wall Street Journal'')]
**A report from the ''[[Irish Times]]'' said that the [[United Nations]] told its employees in a communications guidance to refer to the war in [[Ukraine]] as a "conflict" or "[[military offensive]]" rather than as a "war" or an "[[invasion]]", and also ordered employees to not put the [[Flag of Ukraine|Ukrainian flag]] on any of their [[social media]] accounts to "avoid reputational risk", in an attempt to avoid upsetting [[Russia]]. However, [[Stéphane Dujarric]], spokesman for the [[secretary-general of the United Nations]], wrote in an email to ''[[The Guardian]]'' that no such recommendation was ever issued. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/united-nations-bans-staff-from-using-war-or-invasion-regarding-ukraine-1.4821438 (''The Irish Times'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2022/mar/08/ukraine-news-russia-war-vladimir-putin-volodymyr-zelenskiy-kyiv-russian-invasion-live-latest-updates?page=with:block-622784718f08d64fa95e8a90&filterKeyEvents=false#liveblog-navigation (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**[[2022 Kebbi massacres]]
***[[Bandit]]s in [[Kebbi State]] attack a [[Nigerian Armed Forces|military]] convoy carrying the state's deputy [[governor]], Dabai Yombe. He survives but 19 soldiers are killed. The convoy was making its way to [[Wasagu/Danko]] when the attack occurred. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gunmen-kill-19-soldiers-attack-nigerian-deputy-governors-convoy-2022-03-09/ (Reuters)]
***Gunmen [[ambush]] a team of [[vigilante]]s in Kebbi State, killing a reported 62 people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gunmen-kill-least-62-vigilantes-nigerias-kebbi-state-2022-03-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**An [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province]] [[militant]] [[suicide attack|blows himself up]] in the city of [[Sibi]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. The attack kills five people and injures thirty. It may have been an [[assassination]] attempt on [[President of Pakistan|President]] [[Arif Alvi]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/6475843.html (Voice of America)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**The [[Biden administration]] bans imports of Russian oil, gas and coal to the United States. The United Kingdom also announces that it would phase out Russian oil by the end of the year. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/biden-russia-oil-gas-ban-imports-ukraine/ (CBS)] [https://www.politico.eu/article/uk-to-ban-russian-oil-imports/ (''Politico'')]
**[[government of China|Chinese]] officials indicate that they are interested in buying shares in recently-distressed Russian energy and minerals companies, seeking supply security. The negotiations, however, are still at an early stage. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-08/china-considers-buying-stakes-in-russian-energy-commodity-firms (Bloomberg)]
*Due to the [[panic buying]] of [[nickel]] futures, whose prices have increased above the [[United States dollar|$]]100,000 per tonne mark for the first time, and which doubled for the second consecutive day, the [[London Metal Exchange]] suspends all trading of nickel. [https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/lme-nickel-jumps-another-10-after-record-rally-supply-fears-2022-03-08/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/lme-suspends-nickel-trading-day-after-prices-see-record-run-2022-03-08/ (Reuters 2)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***In an interview with [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]], [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says that [[Ukraine]] is open to holding discussions about the [[International recognition of the Donetsk People's Republic and the Luhansk People's Republic|Russia-recognized]] [[Donetsk People's Republic|Donetsk]] and [[Luhansk People's Republic|Luhansk]] separatist regions in eastern Ukraine. He also concedes that his country may no longer be prepared to be [[Enlargement of NATO|accepted into]] [[NATO]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/ukraines-zelensky-says-he-has-cooled-on-joining-nato-2022-3?amp (''Business Insider'')]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that [[Venezuela]] has freed two [[Americans]], Gustavo Cardenas and Jorge Fernandez, after being detained in the country. [https://www.politico.com/news/2022/03/09/venezuela-release-prisoners-biden-00015501 (''Politico'')]
